subject.title: Add testing framework for cron jobs and skills (dry-run mode)

question: What no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw guarantee for cron and skills test/dry-run, and should it share a request-scoped runtime contract with global agent dry-run?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementing it would define a user-trusted side-effect boundary plus new public CLI, Gateway, protocol, skill-runner, and possible config semantics across tools, hooks, channels, and external APIs.

options.title: Design one request-scoped contract
options.body: Define cron test/validate, skills test, and shared tool-interception semantics together so preview modes make the same side-effect guarantee across runtime paths.

options.title: Ship only a narrow cron validator first
options.body: Add cron config, schedule, and delivery validation while explicitly leaving skills testing and global interception to later decisions.

options.title: Defer broad dry-run semantics
options.body: Keep current command-specific dry-run surfaces until a maintainer sponsors the broader trusted preview boundary.

recommendation.title: Design one request-scoped contract
recommendation.body: Define cron test/validate, skills test, and shared tool-interception semantics together so preview modes make the same side-effect guarantee across runtime paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from current-source blame, prior review context, and feature-history ownership across cron, skills-adjacent CLI, Gateway, and shared tool execution surfaces.
